newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Iraq fears push oil higher, dollar revives.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Iraq fears push oil higher, dollar revives.

text.p: Talk of possible U.S. attacks on Iraq continued to push World oil prices higher on Thursday and the dollar staged a revival against the mark on German rate comments.

On European bourses, leading shares already trading higher after a positive overnight close on Wall Street, were given some backbone by U.S. data showing wholesale prices rose only moderately in August, easing Wall Street fears that a strong economy could ignite inflation.
Benchmark Brent crude futures continued to rally sharply on talk of possible missile or bombing attacks on Iraq by the United States in retaliation against Iraqi attacks on U.S. warplanes.
"We are expecting a U.S. missile attack this afternoon, which will spark the market again," said one broker.
The October Brent contract which expires on Friday, gained 72 cents to $24.30 a barrel, extending gains made after U.S. officials said stealth bombers were heading for the Gulf.
Oil prices were at their highest since Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990 and pushed Brent prices to $40.95.

On the foreign exchange front, the dollar rose to session highs against the mark in the European afternoon after comments from a Bundesbank council member saying he saw more room to cut key German interest rates.

Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher, president of the regional central bank of Berlin and Brandenburg, said rates, including the 2.50-percent discount rate, could fall more if economic conditions permitted, a spokeswoman for the central bank confirmed. The comments were made in an interview on Monday.
The dollar rose to a high of 1.5140 marks but fell short of reclaiming the near-two month high of 1.5155 hit on Wednesday.

"The comments will certainly help the trend that is already in place - for the dollar to go higher," said Stuart Thomson, chief economist at Nikko Europe in London. However, he cautioned Kuehbacher's views are unlikely to reflect the consensus on the policy-making Bundesbank council.

"The consensus seems to be that rates have bottomed and will remain steady for a while since the German economy remains sluggish," said Thomson. He expects another 50 basis points to be cut off the discount rate.

On the London Stock Exchange blue chips edged higher after the benign U.S. inflation data prompted a firmer opening on Wall Street. It had been a busy day in London with results from over 40 companies, including seven from the blue chip FTSE 100 index, few contained unpleasant surprises.
In Paris leading shares forged ahead after the U.S. figures on the back of firmer bonds, the main CAC-40 index was up 24.98 points or 1.22 percent by 1330 GMT.

Frankfurt, which had been less bullish during the day and ended floor trading mixed, rose in post bourse electronic trade following the publication of the U.S. figures. Dealers said sentiment was boosted by firmer government bonds and the strength of the dollar.
CURRENCIES AT 1330 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5113 marks and 109.99 yen compared with late Wednesday's 1.5079 marks and 110.20 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1330 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 20.5 points up at 3,926.1.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 24.98 points up at 2,063.04.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed 3.52 points up at 2,570.32.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was softer at $382.25 compared with its London close on Wednesday of 383.65. Silver fixed at 508.25 cents.
